The user wants a hard technical problem solved: "semantic-anchor checkpoints so an agent's context edit re-prefills only the new suffix, in the Ledger of Empty Chairs game world."

Let me parse this. This is about LLM agent context management — specifically, incremental context editing where instead of re-prefilling the entire context after an edit, you only re-prefill the changed suffix. The mechanism: semantic-anchor checkpoints — points in the context that are semantically stable (immutable, content-addressed) such that edits before/around them don't invalidate the KV cache for everything after them... wait, actually the opposite: anchors partition the context into segments; an edit invalidates only the segment containing it and everything after it in the linear sequence; but if the edit is a suffix append or a local edit within a segment that ends at an anchor boundary... Hmm.

Actually let me think carefully about how KV caching works and what "re-prefill only the new suffix" means.

In transformer inference with prefix caching: the KV cache for tokens 0..n-1 can be reused as long as those exact tokens appear as a prefix of the new prompt. Any edit to token i < n invalidates cache for all tokens ≥ i (because attention is causal and positional embeddings shift). So naive editing of an agent's context (e.g., inserting a tool result mid-conversation, rewriting a memory block) forces full re-prefill.

"Semantic-anchor checkpoints" idea: insert special anchor tokens/markers at semantically stable boundaries. The trick to make suffix-only re-prefill work despite causal attention:

Option A: Anchors reset position ids. If each anchor starts a fresh position space (position 0 within its segment), then segments become independent: KV for segment k depends only on tokens of segment k (plus maybe a fixed anchor header). Then editing any segment invalidates only that segment's KV; other segments' KV blocks remain valid regardless of order. But then cross-segment attention is lost unless you add explicit cross-attention over cached segment summaries — i.e., hierarchical attention: each segment attends to its own tokens plus fixed-size anchor summaries of other segments. That changes the model architecture though. For a game-world agent harness, we can't change the base model weights. So we need something implementable on top of an existing LLM API or local runtime.

Option B: Keep the linear layout but define checkpoints as points where the prefix up to the checkpoint is immutable (content-addressed). Edits are then constrained: any edit must either (a) append after the last checkpoint, or (b) trigger a "checkpoint rewrite" which is amortized. The system maintains a chain of checkpoints C0 < C1 < ... < Ck = current head. Each checkpoint has a hash of the canonical serialization of the context up to that point. When the agent performs a context edit (e.g., prune old turns, inject retrieved lore), the edit is expressed as a patch against the segment between two adjacent checkpoints. If the patch touches segment [Ci, Ci+1), then KV for [0, Ci) is still valid (prefix unchanged), and we re-prefill from Ci onward. That's exactly "re-prefill only the new suffix": the suffix starting at the earliest invalidated checkpoint.

But wait — if you edit inside segment j, everything after segment j also shifts positions, so KV for segments > j is invalid too. So "only the new suffix" = from the start of the edited segment to the end. To make this cheap, you want edits to happen near the tail. The checkpoint discipline enforces that: writes go through a write buffer appended after the last checkpoint; compaction (rewriting history) happens only at checkpoint boundaries and is itself recorded as a new checkpoint event.

Hmm, but there's more nuance: "semantic-anchor" suggests the checkpoints aren't arbitrary token offsets but semantically meaningful units (a closed scene beat, a resolved trade, a sealed ledger entry). In the Ledger of Empty Chairs game world — I need to invent/define this world concretely since it's presumably a fictional setting the user references. It sounds like a game world where there's a "Ledger" tracking "Empty Chairs" — perhaps chairs represent seats/roles/NPCs that have left, debts, unresolved obligations. Let me just define it crisply: Ledger of Empty Chairs (LoEC) is a persistent-state tabletop-ish RPG world where every departure (an NPC leaving a table, a player seat vacated, a promise unfulfilled) is recorded as a ledger entry; the world state advances by entries being opened (chair emptied) and settled (chair refilled/redeemed/forgiven). The agent is the GameMaster/steward whose context contains: world canon, open ledger entries, recent table transcript, and pending actions.

So the deliverable: precise definition of semantic-anchor checkpoints, a schema (JSON/protobuf-ish), and the exact algorithm (data structures + pseudocode) for edit → minimal re-prefill.

Key technical components:

1. Context layout: ordered list of blocks. Each block is typed (CANON, LEDGER_ENTRY, SCENE_BEAT, TOOL_RESULT, POLICY, etc.), immutable once sealed, content-addressed by hash.

2. Semantic anchor: a sealed block boundary that satisfies anchor criteria: (i) closure — the block completes a semantic unit (ledger entry settled, scene beat ended); (ii) immutability — bytes frozen, hash pinned; (iii) referential saturation — no later block depends on the *interior* of this block, only on its anchor handle (id + digest); (iv) determinism — canonical serialization is byte-stable.

3. Checkpoint record: maps anchor id → token offset in the current materialized context, plus prefix hash chain. Because edits invalidate offsets, offsets are recomputed incrementally.

4. Cache management: use prefix caching (e.g., vLLM automatic prefix caching, Anthropic/OpenAI prompt caching with cache_control breakpoints). Place cache breakpoints exactly at anchor boundaries. On edit: compute the lowest invalidated anchor; truncate KV from there; re-prefill suffix = tokens from that anchor to end + new tokens.

Wait — but with provider-side prompt caching, breakpoints are limited (Anthropic allows 4 breakpoints). With local runtimes (vLLM/HF), block-level paged KV reuse works at page granularity (16-token pages typically). So the algorithm should be defined against a generic KV store with page granularity P and prefix-hash addressing like vLLM's hash of (parent_hash, page_tokens). Actually vLLM's prefix caching hashes each block as hash(parent_block_hash || block_token_ids). An edit at token t invalidates the block containing t and all subsequent blocks (since parent chain breaks). Same conclusion: re-prefill from the containing block start. Anchors align blocks to semantic boundaries so that invalidation granularity == semantic granularity, and so that the scheduler can pin hot anchors.

Also need: "re-prefill only the new suffix" — define precisely: given edit e applied to materialized context M producing M', find lcp(M, M') = longest common prefix; suffix S' = M'[|lcp|:]. Re-prefill cost = |S'| tokens. The checkpoint structure guarantees |lcp| ≥ offset(anchor_k) where k = first anchor whose segment is touched. Algorithm: compute first divergence via Merkle-style comparison over segment digests rather than raw tokens (cheap): walk anchors top-down? Actually bottom-up: compare segment digests from anchor list; the first index where digest differs gives divergence point. Since edits are localized, we keep per-segment digests.

Edge cases:
- Edit inserts a whole new segment between anchors: divergence at insertion point.
- Edit rewrites canon early in context: big re-prefill; policy says canon is append-only with supersede entries instead of rewrite, so early edits are forbidden by schema (immutability), replaced by tombstone/supersede records appended later. This is the crucial design move: forbid in-place mutation of anchored regions; all "edits" to semantics are compensating appends. Then divergence point is almost always the write head, and re-prefill is O(suffix).
- Compaction: when context exceeds budget, drop sealed segments from the materialized prompt but keep their anchor handles + digests in a side manifest; replace with a summary block that itself becomes an anchor. Dropping a prefix changes offsets but not validity: the remaining context is a new materialization M2 with its own checkpoint chain seeded from the manifest. Note: dropping a middle segment would break causality for later segments (they attended to it), so compaction may only remove a contiguous prefix (oldest-first) OR replace a contiguous span with a summary inserted at the same start offset — replacing a middle span shifts subsequent tokens, invalidating their KV anyway; allowed but costs re-prefill from that span. Policy: summarize-and-truncate from the front; never splice the middle except at forced re-anchoring events.

Hmm wait, actually replacing a middle span with a shorter summary: tokens after the span shift left → their cached KV is invalid (positions changed). Unless we use position-id remapping... In practice with RoPE, absolute positions matter; shifting invalidates. So rule: compaction ops are (a) prefix-drop, (b) tail-append, (c) full rematerialize (rare, budgeted).

Actually, one more subtlety: prefix-drop changes absolute positions of everything remaining too! If we drop the first 2000 tokens, the remaining tokens now start at position 0 (or whatever the template dictates) and all their cached KV computed under old positions is invalid. Hmm. So prefix-drop also forces full re-prefill under naive absolute positioning.

Solutions:
(a) Keep a stable virtual position space: maintain a position offset map. When materializing the prompt, assign position ids not by physical index but by a monotone virtual coordinate preserved across drops. But standard serving stacks compute positions from token index in the sequence. However, if we control the runtime (local vLLM/HF with custom position_ids input), we can pass explicit position_ids. Many agent frameworks do control this locally. With RoPE, providing position_ids tensor is supported in HF transformers; vLLM supports custom position ids? There's support for MRoPE in Qwen-VL; generic custom position_ids passthrough exists in some paths. Alternatively:

(b) Anchor-relative positioning: each segment restarts positions at 0 (like Option A earlier) — but that breaks cross-segment attention semantics without architectural support... Actually no: if we feed position_ids that continue across segments but are invariant to prefix drops, we need positions to be a function of segment identity, not global index. E.g., position of token = (segment_slot, intra_segment_index) with RoPE treated as 2D... that's again architecture change.

(c) Simplest honest approach used in practice: accept that prefix-drop requires re-prefill of the retained remainder, but make drops rare and amortized: compaction threshold hysteresis, and when it happens, re-prefill is bounded by context budget B, done offline/async while the stale-but-valid cache continues serving reads until the new materialization is warm (double-buffering). Meanwhile, ordinary edits (appends, tail rewrites within the open segment) hit only the suffix.

Hmm, but the user explicitly asks: "context edit re-prefills only the new suffix." So the core guarantee: for the common edit class (append / mutate-open-segment / settle-entry), re-prefill = tokens from divergence anchor to end. And define the edit classes and their costs exactly. Also define the double-buffer for compaction. Good.

Alternatively, there's a cleaner trick for prefix-drop: keep dropped-prefix tokens physically present but masked? No — they'd still occupy positions and compute; wasteful but valid: "tombstone retention": instead of dropping, replace dropped span with nothing... no.

Another approach: sliding-window with sink tokens (StreamingLLM attention sinks) — keep first 4 tokens (sink) + recent window; positions re-based per window. StreamingLLM shows cache reuse with position re-encoding of the window. But that loses long-range fidelity; for a game-world steward we want durable canon. Not appropriate beyond emergency mode.

So final design: 
- Immutable anchored segments (the "sealed ledger").
- One mutable open segment at the tail ("the open chair", nice thematic naming).
- All semantic edits = append compensating records; the only in-place mutation allowed is within the open segment.
- Divergence detection via per-segment content digests (Merkle over segment chain).
- Re-prefill = from divergence anchor offset to end, using provider prefix-cache breakpoints pinned at the last K anchors (K=3 for Anthropic-style 4-breakpoint limit: 1 for system/canon root + 3 rolling anchors; or page-aligned for vLLM).
- Position handling: absolute positions, hence prefix-drop triggers scheduled rematerialization with double-buffered cache swap; guarantee: at most one rematerialization per N tokens appended (amortized O(1) overhead), and rematerialization never runs inline in the turn loop.

Now the Ledger of Empty Chairs world specifics. Define:

World: "Ledger of Empty Chairs" (LoEC) — a persistent multiplayer GM'd world. Core ontology:
- Table: a scene instance with seats.
- Chair: a seat bound to a character/NPC/player. Chair states: FILLED, VACATED (empty), FORFEIT, REDEEMED.
- LedgerEntry: record of a chair transition or obligation. Fields: entry_id, table_id, chair_id, kind (VACATE|PLEDGE|SETTLE|FORFEIT|REDEEM|NOTE), payload, opened_at (world tick), due_tick, status OPEN/SETTLED/WAIVED, dependencies (entry_ids it references), witness hashes.
- Canon: immutable world facts (map, factions, laws of magic), versioned append-only.
- SceneBeat: bounded unit of live play (a exchange of actions/resolutions), ends with a Beat Seal listing affected entries.

The agent = Steward (GM agent). Its context = StewardContext with sections: POLICY (static), CANON_DIGEST (rolling digest + recent canon records), LEDGER_WINDOW (open entries + recently settled), BEAT_BUFFER (current open beat transcript), TOOLS (schemas), SCRATCH (agent notes, mutable).

Semantic anchors in LoEC terms:
- A1 CANON_ANCHOR: after a canon batch is sealed (canon is append-only; seal every T_canon ticks or R records).
- A2 LEDGER_ANCHOR: after a batch of ledger entries reaches quorum/witness closure (all referenced deps SETTLEd or explicitly deferred), entries become immutable → seal.
- A3 BEAT_SEAL: end of scene beat; the beat transcript freezes; a Beat Summary is emitted.
- A4 IDLE_ANCHOR: fallback time/idle-based seal for the open segment if nothing else fires (prevents unbounded open segment).

Anchor criteria (formal): a boundary b is a valid semantic anchor iff:
(i) Closure: the preceding segment realizes a complete semantic unit per its type's seal predicate.
(ii) Determinism: canonical_bytes(segment) is a pure function of the logical records (no timestamps, no dict ordering ambiguity — JCS-like canonical JSON, RFC 8785).
(iii) Referential opacity: all future references to records in this segment use handles (seg_id, rec_id, digest), never interior text spans.
(iv) Stability horizon: probability the segment will be mutated within horizon H is below threshold (estimated from edit-type statistics); enforced structurally by immutability rules rather than predicted — better: structural immutability makes this vacuous; keep as a check for "soft" anchors like scratch notes.

Schema. Give concrete JSON Schema-ish definitions:

Segment {
  seg_id: uuid7 (time-ordered),
  parent_seg_id,
  seq: int (chain index),
  type: enum {POLICY, CANON, LEDGER, BEAT, TOOL, SCRATCH},
  status: OPEN | SEALED | SUPERSEDED,
  records: [Record],
  digest: sha256(canonical_bytes(records)) — content address,
  token_span: [start_tok, end_tok) in current materialization (runtime field, not identity),
  kv_pages: [page_ids] (runtime),
}

Checkpoint {
  cp_id,
  created_seq: seq of last segment included,
  prefix_digest: sha256 over chain of segment digests up to here (Merkle chain: prefix_digest_i = H(prefix_digest_{i-1} || digest_i)),
  token_offset: int (in current materialization),
  cache_key: provider-specific (e.g., anthropic cache breakpoint id / vllm block hash of last page),
  pinned_until_tick,
}

StewardContext materialization M = concat(bytes(seg_0..seg_m)) wrapped in chat template. Template stability matters: the chat template must be deterministic and the segment framing tokens (headers) must be part of the segment bytes so that segment boundaries are token-aligned. Token alignment: ensure each segment begins at a token boundary — trivially true since we tokenize concatenated text; but for page-aligned caching, pad segment headers to page multiples? vLLM caches at block granularity with hashing of exact block contents; misalignment just means the boundary block is shared partially — fine, hashing handles it. For Anthropic-style explicit breakpoints, breakpoints are message-level, so put each sealed segment in its own message (or group) and set cache_control on the last message of each anchored group. Constraint: ≤4 breakpoints → keep at most 3 sealed anchor groups + 1 tail. Older sealed groups get folded into a running digest line (one short message) — "fold": replace segments s_i..s_j with FoldMarker{from,to,prefix_digest} — but folding shifts tokens → invalidates suffix → do folds only right before a scheduled rematerialization, or accept fold cost. Better: fold during rematerialization only.

Algorithm. State: 
- SegmentChain: ordered list of segments (logical, immutable once sealed).
- Materializer: renders chain → token list with offsets per segment.
- CacheManager: tracks valid KV ranges; knows provider granularity.
- EditLog: incoming edits.

Edit types and their handling:
E_APPEND(recs): append to OPEN segment (or create new segment if open just sealed). Divergence = start of open segment? No—append extends the tail; if the open segment had prior cached tokens, appending changes only bytes after previous end → divergence = old end offset = token_offset(open.start)+len(prev bytes)... careful: appending to the open segment keeps its earlier bytes identical, so LCP = end of previous materialization. Re-prefill = new tokens only. 
E_SEAL(type): seal open segment if predicate holds → creates anchor; no byte change except appending the seal footer (anchor marker + digest line) → re-prefill = footer tokens only. Then optionally rotate cache breakpoint to this anchor.
E_MUTATE_SCRATCH(new_scratch_bytes): scratch is the one mutable region; it sits at the tail (after all sealed segments, before/within open segment). Mutation rewrites scratch → divergence = scratch start → re-prefill = scratch + open tail. Keep scratch small (budget S_max tokens) to bound this.
E_SETTLE(entry_id): logically mutates a ledger entry's status. Forbidden in place if entry is in a sealed segment → emit compensating record SETTLE_REF{entry_id, digest_expected} appended to open LEDGER segment. The renderer, when materializing, applies compensation overlay: sealed bytes stay byte-identical; the overlay lives in the open segment (a compact "Ledger Delta" block listing status flips). So the sealed text still shows old status?? That's bad for the model reading it. Solution: renderer emits sealed ledger entries with status field rendered as of a snapshot? No—bytes must be stable. Instead: sealed entries render without live status; status is carried solely in the Ledger Delta overlay in the open segment. I.e., sealed LEDGER segment stores immutable facts (who, what, when, obligations), and all mutable state (status) lives in the delta overlay. That preserves both immutability and correctness. 

E_COMPACT(trigger): when total tokens > H_high: build new chain: [POLICY(root, unchanged)] + [FOLD digest summary of dropped sealed segments] + retained recent sealed segments + open. Rematerialize, prefill fully in shadow buffer, atomic swap. Cost B tokens, amortized: happens at most once per (H_high − H_low) appended tokens.

Divergence computation: given previous materialization M and next M', compute d = length of longest common token prefix. Efficient method: compare segment-by-segment using stored digests: walk segments in order; for identical seg_id+digest, add its token length; stop at first mismatch or at the open segment (compare its rendered bytes/token prefix directly, or simply treat open segment as divergent-from-its-mutation-point: track open segment's committed prefix length = bytes already cached). Simpler operational rule: maintain `cached_upto` pointer = token offset through which KV is valid. After each successful prefill, cached_upto = len(M). On edit, compute new M'; d = LCP(M, M'); invalidate (cached_upto = d); prefill M'[d:] (with provider prefix cache, you just send the full M' with breakpoints; provider reuses cached pages automatically — the algorithm's job is to place breakpoints at anchors and keep bytes stable so the provider's block hashes match).

Important: with provider-side prefix caching (vLLM APC, Anthropic), you don't manually manage KV; you ensure byte-stability and set breakpoints. The "algorithm" then is: (1) keep sealed bytes frozen; (2) put breakpoints at anchor boundaries; (3) order materialization so the volatile stuff is last; (4) measure LCP to report/verify savings. With self-hosted manual KV (HF + past_key_values), you literally slice: past_kv[:, :, :d] reused, prefill tokens M'[d:] with correct position_ids offset d. Provide both paths.

Position ids for sliced prefill: pos = d + arange(len(suffix)). Works because prefix bytes identical ⇒ same positions. 

Cache eviction/pinning: pin pages covering last W anchors (W=3) + policy root; evict others under pressure (they're recoverable via re-prefill from nearest surviving anchor... actually evicting a middle anchor's pages doesn't force immediate re-prefill; it forces re-prefill from the previous surviving anchor on next request. Track `valid_from` = furthest anchor whose pages are all resident.)

Correctness argument sketch: 
Lemma 1 (Prefix determinism): sealed segment bytes are a pure function of (type, records) under canonical encoding; hence equal digests ⇒ equal token bytes under fixed tokenizer/template. 
Lemma 2 (Causal locality): transformer KV for positions < d depends only on tokens < d. Hence if LCP(M,M')=d, KV[0:d] remains exactly valid for M'. 
Therefore reusing KV[0:d] and prefilling M'[d:] yields bit-identical logits to full prefill. Anchors exist to (a) maximize expected d under the edit distribution, (b) give provider-aligned breakpoints, (c) bound the search for d to O(#segments) digest comparisons instead of token diff.

Cost accounting: E[re-prefill] = E[len(M') − d]. Under rules: appends cost ~append size; scratch mutations cost ≤ S_max; settles cost ~delta size; seals cost ~footer; compaction costs B once per (H_high−H_low). Compare baseline: every edit costs full |M'|. Give numbers example: B=32k, typical turn append 400 tok, scratch 512, delta 128 → per-turn re-prefill ≈ 500–1000 tok vs 32k baseline; compaction amortized adds B/(H_high−H_low) ≈ 32k/24k ≈ 1.33 tok/token overhead... hmm that's if H_high−H_low=8k, 32k/8k=4x. Choose H_high=40k, H_low=24k → 32k/16k = 2 tok per appended tok worst case; but compaction can be async/off-critical-path, so latency unaffected; throughput cost only.

Seal predicates (exact):
- BEAT seal: open beat has ≥1 completed exchange AND (tick_since_open ≥ T_beat OR participant idle flag OR beat_closed_by_tool). 
- LEDGER seal: all records in open ledger segment reference only SETTLEd-or-deferred deps, and segment age ≥ T_ledger or count ≥ R_ledger.
- CANON seal: canon batch closed by canon_commit tool call (explicit).
- IDLE seal: open segment age ≥ T_idle regardless (force anchor so divergence point never drifts too far back).

Parameters table: P (kv page)=16, W (pinned anchors)=3, S_max=512, T_beat=…, etc. Give defaults.

Failure modes & guards:
- Template drift (upgrading chat template invalidates all caches) → template_version in checkpoint; mismatch ⇒ full rematerialize.
- Tokenizer drift similarly.
- Non-deterministic rendering (timestamps) → ban wall-clock in sealed bytes; use world tick.
- Provider cache eviction → valid_from tracking; degrade gracefully.
- Mid-segment provider breakpoint limit (≤4) → rolling window of breakpoints; older anchors rely on natural block-hash sharing (vLLM) even without explicit breakpoint.
- Race: edit arrives during prefill → serialize via single-writer turn loop; edits queue.
- Hash collision → ignore (sha256).
- Open segment grows unbounded if seal predicates never fire → IDLE seal caps it at T_idle·rate; also hard cap C_open tokens forcing seal-or-split.

Verification hook: after each serve, recompute digest of sent prefix vs checkpoint chain; assert match; on mismatch, log CACHE_INVALIDATION event and fall back to full prefill. Also periodic shadow full-prefill (every Nth turn) comparing logits/KL to sliced path to catch silent staleness (should be none by Lemma 2, but catches implementation bugs like template nondeterminism).

Now the "Ledger of Empty Chairs" flavor: name components thematically but keep engineering precision: 
- The context is "the seating chart"; sealed segments are "chairs that no longer get rewritten" — an empty chair = a sealed slot whose occupant (content) has departed; the ledger records departures/settlements. Anchors = "chair bolts." Eh — keep flavor light: define world entities because the schema needs concrete record types, and show worked examples of edits (vacate → pledge → settle) flowing through the pipeline with token counts.

Worked micro-example: 
Segments: POLICY(180 tok, sealed forever), CANON#1(900, sealed), LEDGER#1(600, sealed, 12 entries), BEAT#7(1400, sealed), OPEN_LEDGER_DELTA(120, open), SCRATCH(300, open), BEAT#8-in-progress(250, open). Total ≈ 3750. Breakpoints at CANON#1, LEDGER#1, BEAT#7 (+tail implicit). Player action causes: tool result (90 tok) appended to open beat; settle of entry E-114 (delta +14 tok); scratch update (+40). New materialization differs only after offset of SCRATCH start? Wait: order matters — put SCRATCH before open beat? If scratch mutates and beat appends, divergence = min(start(scratch), …) = start(scratch) → re-prefill = scratch(340) + beat-open(340) ≈ 680 tok vs 3750 full. Alternatively order: sealed, open-beat, scratch-last → scratch mutation re-prefills only scratch (300) but then scratch sits after beat so beat text precedes notes — acceptable? Notes-at-end is fine, even desirable (recency). Rule: order segments by volatility: most-volatile last. Volatility order: POLICY < CANON < LEDGER(sealed) < BEAT(sealed) < LEDGER_DELTA(open) < BEAT_OPEN < SCRATCH. But LEDGER_DELTA open and BEAT_OPEN interleave logically... The delta overlay must be readable near ledger? Not necessary — it's a state table; put all open state in one "OPEN STATE" segment at tail: [OPEN_LEDGER_DELTA][BEAT_OPEN][SCRATCH]. Mutations to any sub-part re-prefill the tail from the earliest mutated sub-part; since all are in the tail cluster, cost ≤ tail size. Bound tail budget T_tail=2048; exceeding forces seal of the oldest open sub-part (seal moves it leftward into anchored region — sealing appends a copy into a new sealed segment and removes from tail? Removal shifts bytes → invalidates tail only, which is cheap since tail is small. Nice: seal operation = promote out of tail; cost = re-prefill of remaining tail (~small). 

So refined layout: [ROOT: policy+template][ANCHORED: sealed segments in fixed order][TAIL: open state cluster]. All edits touch TAIL except compaction/fold. Therefore steady-state re-prefill ≤ |TAIL| + append. Guarantee: re-prefill tokens per turn ≤ T_tail + max_append, with T_tail=2048 default. That's the crisp theorem-ish statement.

Define LCP-check algorithm precisely:

function apply_edits(chain, edits):
  # 1. classify
  for e in edits: route(e)
  # appends/mutations target TAIL segments only; anything targeting sealed seg → convert to compensating record appended to TAIL (or reject per policy)
  # 2. seal sweep
  while seal_predicate(open_subsegment) or tail_tokens > T_tail: promote_oldest()
  # 3. render
  M' = render(chain)   # deterministic
  d = lcp_tokens(M_prev, M')  # via segment digests + tail byte diff
  # 4. serve
  if provider_prefix_cache: send M' with breakpoints at last W sealed anchors; provider dedups
  else: kv = kv[:d]; prefill(M'[d:], position_offset=d)
  M_prev = M'; checkpoint.update(offsets)

lcp via digests: iterate segments; while seg.sealed and seg.digest==stored.digest: d += seg.token_len; then within tail, byte-compare rendered tail prefix (cheap, tail small) to find exact d. Store per-render token lengths.

Compaction (fold) algorithm:
trigger: total_tokens > H_high.
build fold: choose cut c = newest anchor such that tokens_before(c) ≥ H_low_target... Actually we drop oldest sealed segments up to cut, replacing with FOLD marker carrying (range, prefix_digest, summary_digest). New chain = [POLICY][FOLD][sealed(c..)][TAIL]. Render M_new; full prefill into shadow KV; verify digest chain continuity (fold.prefix_digest links old chain so historical proofs still verify); atomic swap M_prev=M_new, kv=shadow. Frequency bound: once per ≥(H_high−H_low) appended tokens.

Also define checkpoint persistence: checkpoints are durable (survive restart): store {chain file (records), template_version, tokenizer_version}; KV cache itself may be lost → on restart, valid_from=0, full prefill once; anchors still minimize future invalidations. Optionally persist KV pages if runtime supports (vLLM doesn't across restarts; fine).

Schema: provide actual JSON Schema (concise but complete) for Segment, Record variants (VacateRecord, PledgeRecord, SettleRecord, ForfeitRecord, RedeemNoteRecord, CanonRecord, BeatEvent, ToolResult, ScratchPatch, SettleRef, FoldMarker), Checkpoint, Manifest. Use RFC 8785 canonical JSON for digests. IDs: uuidv7. Digests: hex sha256.

Also specify the exact prompt-template framing: each segment rendered as:

<seg id="..." t="LEDGER" d="ab12…" n="12">
…records…
</seg>

Header includes digest so the model can cite handles; footer for sealed: </seg> plus anchor line: ⚓ ANCHOR cp=… pdigest=…. Must be careful: including digest in header means digest must be computed over records only (not header) to avoid circularity — specify: digest = H(canonical(records)); header carries it; fine.

Token-alignment note: no requirement that segments align to tokenizer pages; provider block hashing handles arbitrary boundaries; explicit breakpoints (Anthropic) are message-boundary based → map each anchor group to message boundary: materialization uses one assistant/system message per zone: msg0=ROOT, msg1..msgk=sealed groups (breakpoints on last k), msgTail=open. Anthropic allows marking up to 4 blocks; set cache_control on ROOT and last 3 sealed messages. Tail uncached (it changes). Actually you'd want cache_control also enabling incremental writes; each cached block accumulates; fine.

Now also handle "re-prefill only the new suffix" claim precisely with the two provider modes:
Mode A (self-hosted, manual KV): literal slice; savings exact.
